title: Diosmetin suppresses the progression of ESCC by CDK2/Rb/E2F2/RRM2 pathway and synergies with cisplatin.
authors: Chen, Yihuan; Dai, Xiaoshuo; Chen, Wei; Qiao, Yan; Bai, Ruihua; Duan, Xiaoxuan; Zhang, Kai; Chen, Xinhuan; Li, Xin; Mo, Saijun; Cao, Wenbo; Li, Xiang; Liu, Kangdong; Dong, Ziming; Lu, Jing
one_liner_zh: 该文研究药物Diosmetin通过CDK2/Rb/E2F2/RRM2通路抑制食管鳞癌，虽涉及E2F2转录因子对RRM2的调控及分子对接，但核心是肿瘤药理学与肾毒性保护，非蛋白质-DNA互作机制建模，方法上仅简单对接，无AI或MD深度建模。
abstract: Cisplatin (CDDP) is the first-line drug in the clinical treatment of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC), which has severe nephrotoxicity. Diosmetin (DIOS) can protect kidney from oxidative damage, however, its function in ESCC is unknown. This study aims to explore the effect and mechanism of DIOS on ESCC and its combined effect with CDDP. Herein, we found that DIOS significantly inhibited the progression of ESCC in vitro and in vivo. Furthermore, the anti-tumor effect of DIOS was not statistically different from that of CDDP. Mechanically, transcriptomics revealed that DIOS inhibited the E2F2/RRM2 signaling pathway. The transcriptional regulation of RRM2 by E2F2 was verified by luciferase assay. Moreover, docking model, CETSA, pull-down assay and CDK2 inhibitor assay confirmed that DIOS directly targeted CDK2, leading to significant suppression of ESCC. Additionally, the patient-derived xenografts (PDX) model showed that the combination of DIOS and CDDP significantly inhibited the growth of ESCC. Importantly, the combined treatment with DIOS and CDDP significantly reduced the mRNA expression levels of kidney injury biomarkers KIM-1 and NGAL in renal tissue, as well as the levels of blood urea nitrogen, serum creatinine and blood uric acid compared to the single treatment with CDDP. In conclusion, DIOS could be an effective drug and a potential chemotherapeutic adjuvant for ESCC treatment. Furthermore, DIOS could reduce the nephrotoxicity of CDDP to some extent.
abstract_zh: 顺铂（CDDP）是临床治疗食管鳞状细胞癌（ESCC）的一线药物，但其具有严重的肾毒性。香叶木素（DIOS）可保护肾脏免受氧化损伤，然而其在ESCC中的作用尚不清楚。本研究旨在探讨DIOS对ESCC的作用及其机制，以及其与CDDP的联合效应。本研究发现，DIOS在体外和体内均显著抑制了ESCC的进展。此外，DIOS的抗肿瘤效果与CDDP相比无统计学差异。机制上，转录组学揭示DIOS抑制了E2F2/RRM2信号通路。通过荧光素酶实验验证了E2F2对RRM2的转录调控。此外，分子对接模型、CETSA、pull-down实验及CDK2抑制剂实验证实，DIOS直接靶向CDK2，从而显著抑制ESCC。另外，患者来源异种移植（PDX）模型显示，DIOS与CDDP联合使用显著抑制了ESCC的生长。重要的是，与单独使用CDDP相比，DIOS与CDDP联合治疗显著降低了肾组织中肾损伤生物标志物KIM-1和NGAL的mRNA表达水平，以及血尿素氮、血清肌酐和血尿酸的水平。总之，DIOS可能是治疗ESCC的有效药物及潜在的化疗辅助剂。此外，DIOS在一定程度上可减轻CDDP的肾毒性。
